answer: Each identity locks an 80-credit ferrous bond and registers one key-bound snowmelt gauge. At dawn the gauge publishes its runoff reading; the first gauge fee is 28 credits, the kth 28+6(k-1), so the 1,000th costs 6,022 and 1,000 fakes pay 3,025,000 in fees plus 80,000 locked. At zenith an auditor recomputes runoff from the public snowpack table and temperature log; a mismatched reading burns the bond. A rented-gauge ring fails: one serial filed under a second key burns both bonds. An honest operator pays 28 once and recovers the bond after a clean window.
